OriginalProposition: A place, centre or minimum stay is not guaranteed.
Notes: Removed unsupported placement/minimum-stay guarantee caveat; preceding sentence says a stay may be offered and is capped, so removal does not promise placement or a minimum stay.

OriginalProposition: The UCTAT email address is a query contact, not an accommodation application form.
FinalProposition: The Government lists ukrainetempaccom@equality.gov.ie as UCTAT’s contact for accommodation or family queries.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: The UCTAT email address is not a guarantee of accommodation placement.
Notes: Removed unsupported no-placement-guarantee caveat. The contact is now described only as the official accommodation-query route.

OriginalProposition: The homelessness service decides what help is available.
FinalProposition: In Dublin, contact the Dublin Region Homeless Executive; elsewhere, contact the local authority for information about local homelessness services.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: Private renting is separate from State accommodation and from social housing.
FinalProposition: HAP is a separate local-authority payment for eligible households renting privately.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: A TP permission is not a tenancy agreement.
FinalProposition: RTB provides tenancy-agreement templates to record the terms between landlords and tenants.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: Applying for or viewing a rental property does not guarantee that the landlord will offer a tenancy.
Notes: Removed unsupported no-tenancy-offer guarantee caveat; the article explains the tenancy agreement process and does not promise an offer.

OriginalProposition: It does not establish a universal immigration-document requirement.
Notes: Removed nonessential negative about a universal immigration-document rule; the RTB checklist remains scoped to rent and tenancy details.

OriginalProposition: Neither the 30-day nor 90-day period promises indefinite housing.
Notes: Removed the nonessential no-indefinite-housing caveat; the article states the official cohort-specific maximum durations directly.

OriginalProposition: Neither the 30-day nor 90-day period promises a chosen centre.
Notes: Removed unsupported preferred-centre guarantee caveat; the article describes the policy and its named short-stay centres without promising choice.

OriginalProposition: Government announced that phased withdrawal of State-contracted commercial accommodation began in August 2026.
FinalProposition: The Government’s phased withdrawal of State-contracted commercial accommodation began in August 2026.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: The announced March 2027 completion date is a programme target, not an individual legal-expiry date.
FinalProposition: The Government’s target is to complete the phased withdrawal of State-contracted commercial accommodation by March 2027.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: Residents are to receive notice.
FinalProposition: The Government says residents affected by the commercial-accommodation withdrawal will be notified before their accommodation changes.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: Residents are to receive support.
FinalProposition: The Government says the Irish Red Cross and IOM will provide information and support to residents moving towards independent living.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: People who need ongoing State accommodation may apply through UCTAT with reasons and supporting evidence.
FinalProposition: People who find self-sufficiency difficult may apply to UCTAT for continued State accommodation and provide reasons and supporting evidence.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: Another centre or location may be used for ongoing State accommodation.
FinalProposition: Continued State accommodation may be in a different location and setting.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: Tenancy type and legal exceptions affect the one-month advance-rent limit.
FinalProposition: For student-specific accommodation, advance rent above one month is allowed only when rent and tuition are paid to the same provider and the landlord agrees.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: The 90-day maximum is not a guarantee of an unused or minimum stay.
FinalProposition: People granted TP before 10 November 2025 who seek State accommodation remain entitled to a maximum of 90 days in a Designated Accommodation Centre.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: Compulsory education generally applies from age six until age 16 or completion of three years of post-primary education, whichever is later.
FinalProposition: For a child under 18, compulsory education applies from age six until age 16 or completion of three years of post-primary education, whichever is later.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.

OriginalProposition: Higher-education institutions decide programme requirements.
Notes: Removed general institution-decides-programme-requirements statement; the article retains specific CAO and SUSI procedures and no admission promise.

OriginalProposition: Higher-education credit transfer is assessed separately.
Notes: Removed nonessential credit-transfer generalisation; the remaining article explains CAO, recognition, temporary tuition support and SUSI separately.

OriginalProposition: TESS may assist with school-admission issues.
FinalProposition: TESS is the statutory agency that can assist parents experiencing difficulty securing a school place for their child.
Notes: Exact existing official source supports the unchanged proposition.

OriginalProposition: Other schemes have separate conditions.
Notes: Removed generic transition sentence; the following text already describes Basic SWA, Jobseeker’s Allowance and Additional Needs Payment separately.

OriginalProposition: The current reach of the 2022 HRC approach across schemes and new section 237 permissions is unresolved.
FinalProposition: Section 237(11)(b) provides for the same social-welfare benefits as Irish citizens on the same conditions, except while the person is resident in designated premises.
Notes: Exact proposition supported by newly audited official source.
